methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting the technology gap in Hampton Roads represent grassroots skill-building infrastructure that could enable distributed, peer-to-peer learning beyond elite institutions—a critical test of whether deep capability can spread through community networks rather than concentrating in university hubs.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership signals institutional concentration of AI education resources in Richmond's urban core, likely creating metro-level depth but raising questions about whether capability radiates outward or remains anchored to university-adjacent talent pools.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce without corresponding depth-building suggests shallow, anxiety-driven adoption rather than genuine capability development—workers feeling displacement risk without acquiring the deep skills to navigate or lead AI transformation.

signals.title: Norfolk could get AI assist for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk's AI dispatcher for non-emergency calls exemplifies platform-delivered automation requiring minimal local AI literacy—broad functional adoption through turnkey solutions that distributes immediate benefits but not the underlying capability to build, customize, or innovate.

signals.title: Virginia Beach schools bring ChatGPT under division oversight as AI use grows - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach schools bringing ChatGPT under district oversight reflects reactive governance of consumer AI tools rather than proactive capability-building—distributed access through commercial platforms without corresponding investment in deep technical literacy or local model development.
